chunk_findings.detail: `_fixed_in_window` counts any bug whose `fixed_at` is within the window, but it never checks `b.open` or the bug’s resolution. Given a reopened bug record with `open=True` and a still-populated `fixed_at`, `vigil` adds that same bug to both `open_total` and `fixed_in_window`. The function docstring says “Bugs closed as fixed,” so the condition should exclude open/reopened bugs, e.g. require `not b.open`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/vigil.py:_fixed_in_window

chunk_findings.detail: The intent requires reviewer reachability to be classified as `up/429/slow`, but `_reviewer_rows` only ever emits `"up"`, `"down"`, or `"429"`. Every reviewer with an entry in `RVM.degraded_marks(st)` is hard-coded to reachability `"429"`, so a reviewer degraded for latency/slowness is reported under the 429/quota bucket, and `_render` can never display a slow reviewer line. The compact snapshot therefore returns the wrong reachability class for slow-but-quota-ok reviewers.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/vigil.py:_reviewer_rows

chunk_findings.detail: The requested snapshot is reviewer reachability `up` / `429` / `slow`. `_reviewer_rows` only emits `up`, `down`, or `429` from `degraded_marks` and `_url_ok`. A reviewer that answers but is slow (the case `reviewer_latency_ratio` is meant to surface) is still reported `up` with an empty reason, so the hourly block never distinguishes slow from healthy. `now` is accepted and unused, so marks are not aged either.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/vigil.py:_reviewer_rows

chunk_findings.detail: `PN.regenerate(..., check=True)` and `RVM.load_reviewers` are wrapped in bare `except Exception: return []`. If pin regeneration raises (bad config, unreadable pin dir) or reviewer load fails, vigil returns `stale_pins: []` / `reviewers: []` and `_render` prints `stale pins: none` and an empty reviewer list. That is the same shape as a clean tree, so the coordinator’s one-call snapshot reports health when the check did not run.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/vigil.py:_stale_pins

chunk_findings.detail: The slow-reachability classification is still not per reviewer. `_reviewer_rows` takes a single scalar `slow` from `FSX.reviewer_latency_ratio` and, for every enabled reviewer whose URL is up, emits `"slow"` whenever that aggregate scalar is > 1.0, otherwise `"up"`; the `now` argument is unused. Given two answering reviewers, one faster than usual and one slower than usual, the aggregate can be > 1.0 and both rows are reported `"slow"`; if the aggregate is <= 1.0, the actually slow reviewer is reported `"up"`. The snapshot therefore returns wrong per-reviewer up/429/slow reachability, not the classification the intent requires.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/vigil.py:_reviewer_rows

chunk_findings.detail: The new `vigil` command advertises contradictory reviewer reachability classes: `summary` says `up/429/slow`, while `description` says `up/down/429`. One of these user-facing strings is wrong about what the snapshot returns, so `ddflow help vigil` will misdescribe the output for either slow or down reviewers.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/health.py:20,27

chunk_findings.detail: The new regression test stubs the exact helpers that produce two of the six required snapshot fields: `_stale_pins` is replaced with `lambda repo, cfg: []` and `_reviewer_rows` with a constant `up` row before `VV.vigil` is called. A broken `vigil` implementation that swallowed pin-check errors and always reported `stale_pins: []`, or one that never reported the required `slow` reachability, would still pass `test_vigil_reports_severities_lanes_and_a_reviewer_line` because the test replaces those functions with the expected output, so this regression test does not actually guard the stale-pins or reviewer-reachability portions of the bug.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_vigil.py:26-28

chunk_findings.detail: `slow` is one fleet-wide `reviewer_latency_ratio`, then every answering reviewer is labeled from that single number. Given two enabled reviewers both passing `_url_ok`, and `reviewer_latency_ratio == 2.5` because only reviewer A was slow, both rows get `reachability: "slow"`. A healthy reviewer is reported in the slow bucket, so the snapshot still does not classify reachability per reviewer as up / 429 / slow.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/vigil.py:_reviewer_rows

chunk_findings.detail: The snapshot still does not return the requested `up/429/slow` reviewer reachability. `_reviewer_rows` emits only `"up"`, `"down"`, or `"429"`; it never emits `"slow"`. `slow` is only the fleet-wide scalar `reviewer_latency_ratio` in `vigil`. Given two enabled reviewers A and B whose URLs both answer (`_url_ok` true) and `FSX.reviewer_latency_ratio(events, now)` is 2.5 because A is slow, the rows are `A: up`, `B: up`; A is reported as reachable `up` rather than `slow`. The requirement from B3a86c5cfb9 is per-reviewer `up/429/slow`, so the fix still misses that field.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/vigil.py:_reviewer_rows

chunk_findings.detail: The new `vigil` command’s user-facing strings promise reviewer reachability classes `up/down/429`, but the change’s own intent for B3a86c5cfb9 requires `up/429/slow`. `ddflow help vigil` therefore misdescribes the snapshot: it tells readers a reviewer row can be `down` and omits the actual required `slow` class. The summary and description should say `up/429/slow`, not `up/down/429`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/health.py:20,27

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier test-stub concern is only partly answered: the test no longer replaces `_reviewer_rows`, but it still never puts a reviewer into the required `slow` reachability state. It seeds one reachable reviewer and asserts only `r["reachability"] in ("up", "429")`; an implementation whose `_reviewer_rows` always returns `"up"` for enabled reviewers would pass this test, so the regression test would not catch the bug’s slow-reachability failure condition.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_vigil.py:57

chunk_findings.detail: With no enabled reviewers, `_reviewer_rows` returns `[]`, and `_render` still emits `reviewers: ` (empty suffix) and then skips the row block because `if data["reviewers"]` is false for an empty list. `None` is the only case labeled `unavailable`, so a configured fleet of zero reviewers is printed as a truncated line rather than `none`. A coordinator reading the CLI text cannot tell "nobody enabled" from a cut-off snapshot. Data JSON keeps `[]`, so only the prose surface is wrong.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/vigil.py:_render
